tagline: Up out of the canyon onto a lid of old lava.
intro: From I-70 the road follows the canyon of Plateau Creek to the town of Mesa, then climbs the steep north side past Powderhorn into evergreen forest and out onto the top of the Grand Mesa, about 11,000 feet up. It crosses the top among its lakes and comes down the south slope to Cedaredge in the Surface Creek Valley.

The mesa wears a cap of basalt from at least 27 lava flows that filled an old valley some ten million years ago. The hard rock held while the rivers cut away everything around it. What was once the lowest ground is now the highest.

moments.title: Grand Mesa
moments.text: More than 300 lakes lie scattered over the top, many of them reservoirs for drinking and irrigation water, and they hold rainbow, cutthroat and brook trout.

moments.title: Land's End Observatory
moments.text: About ten miles off the highway, a 1930s ranger observatory of fitted mesa basalt stands on the rim. Two hundred out-of-work veterans built much of the road there at a dollar a day.

moments.title: Cedaredge
moments.text: A farm town under the south slope of the mesa, raising beef cattle, elk, apples and peaches, with a view south to the San Juan Mountains.

practical: Services between Cedaredge and Mesa are limited. Land's End Road is about half gravel, and the observatory building itself was closed and boarded up as of 2022.
